Puerto Williams is situated on Chile's Navarino Island, on the shore of the Beagle Channel. Its small harbor, low-rise houses, and forested slopes give the remote southern settlement its distinctive appearance. Beyond the town, the island's mountains rise toward the hiking routes of the Dientes de Navarino area.

The town features on voyages through the southern channels and on routes toward Cape Horn. Between long passages at sea, it offers a glimpse of the inhabited side of Tierra del Fuego. A walk along the waterfront depends on the vessel's schedule and landing conditions. Expect the region's cool, windy, and changeable weather.
